articles.title: ‘A long journey’: Ottawa Senators’ Tyler Boucher finally gets his NHL debut after battling years of setbacks
articles.summary: Tyler Boucher, drafted 10th overall by the Ottawa Senators in 2021, finally debuts in the NHL after years of injuries and setbacks, showcasing perseverance and determination to reach his dream.
articles.body: Tyler Boucher is finally getting the opportunity he has chased since the Ottawa Senators selected him 10th overall in the 2021 NHL Draft. After four surgeries and several injury-plagued seasons, the 23-year-old forward has been recalled from the Belleville Senators ahead of his NHL debut against the Winnipeg Jets.The milestone is all the more meaningful for Boucher’s family, including his father, former NHL goaltender Brian Boucher. This is a story of perseverance, rehabilitation, and determination through years of injuries to reach his dream of playing in the NHL.Tyler Boucher finally earns Ottawa Senators NHL opportunityTyler Boucher is set to make his long-awaited NHL debut with the Ottawa Senators after years of battling injuries and setbacks. His opportunity comes following winger Hayden Hodgson's groin injury during Ottawa's 4-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.Boucher was called up from the Belleville Senators, Ottawa’s American Hockey League affiliate, to fill the roster spot and is expected to join Stephen Halliday and Sammy Blais on the fourth line against the Winnipeg Jets.The call-up is huge for the forward who has waited more than five years since being picked 10th overall in the 2021 NHL Draft.Why has Tyler Boucher faced so many setbacks?Boucher’s career has been marred by injuries, including four surgeries that stalled his development and minutes.Drafted in 2021, he’s played two injury-plagued seasons with the Ontario Hockey League’s Ottawa 67’s. He also faced challenges with his transition to the American Hockey League, as staying healthy was a recurring obstacle.Boucher, however, kept chasing his NHL dream. He has shown promising signs this season with Belleville.Before the call-up, he had five goals and 10 points in 17 games. He also scored in Belleville's 3-1 win over Cleveland on Sunday, giving the organization another reason to think about him for the opening.His father, Brian, said he was proud of his son's determination and his ability to overcome difficult circumstances. He stressed perseverance, resilience, and the fight it takes to keep chasing an NHL career through repeated injuries. Through his recoveries, the family had been behind Tyler and invested in his ambition to represent Ottawa.It’s a good opportunity for him, Senators head coach Travis Green also said. He admitted that Boucher had previously been prevented from being called up because of injuries.Boucher kept getting better as a player in tough circumstances, Green said. He added that he hopes the NHL debut is the start of a longer tenure with the organization.For Boucher, the chance is more than a first NHL appearance. It’s the reward for years of rehab, patience, and persistence after a rocky start to his pro career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sidney Crosby's Pittsburgh Penguins future enters an uncertain phase as Kyle Dubas prepares for possible NHL roster changes
articles.summary: Explore the uncertainties surrounding Sidney Crosby's future with the Pittsburgh Penguins as GM Kyle Dubas prepares for potential roster changes amid a rocky season.
articles.body: The Pittsburgh Penguins are facing important decisions about their veteran core, with captain Sidney Crosby's future becoming a central question. General manager Kyle Dubas is reportedly willing to honor Crosby's wishes, whether he chooses to continue in Pittsburgh, retire, or request a trade.The 39-year-old center is in the final months of his deal, and the Penguins' rocky start has raised questions about the direction of the franchise. Crosby has spent his entire 22-season NHL career with Pittsburgh, making his next decision particularly significant for the organization and its supporters.Sidney Crosby's Pittsburgh Penguins future remains in his handsSidney Crosby will have the final say over his future with the Pittsburgh Penguins, according to The Athletic's Josh Yohe. General manager Kyle Dubas is reportedly prepared to accommodate the captain's wishes, even if that means arranging a trade.Yohe explained in his November 16 report that Pittsburgh would not force Crosby into a particular outcome. If the veteran center wants to continue playing for the Penguins beyond the 2026-27 season, the organization is expected to make that possible. Retirement would also be respected, while a trade request would prompt Dubas to explore a deal.Sidney Crosby's contract situation adds to Pittsburgh's uncertaintyCrosby's current contract expires after the 2026-27 NHL season. The 39-year-old signed a two-year, $17.4 million contract with an average annual value of $8.7 million in September. Through 20 games, he has recorded 13 points, according to recent reporting, while Pittsburgh has struggled to establish consistency.Despite the difficult start, Crosby continues to add to his historic NHL achievements. Earlier in November, he moved past Marcel Dionne into sixth place on the league's all-time points list.Evgeni Malkin also faces an uncertain Penguins futureCrosby is not the only Pittsburgh veteran whose future could become a major talking point. Evgeni Malkin is also approaching the end of his contract, and the 40-year-old center could face a similar decision about his next career move.According to Yohe, the Penguins are comfortable allowing Malkin to finish the 2026-27 season in Pittsburgh. Any potential trade would require his approval, meaning the defenseman would have considerable control over his next destination.Yohe believes Karlsson could consider joining a legitimate Stanley Cup contender despite his contractual protection. Such a move would potentially give the veteran another opportunity to compete for the championship that has remained missing from his NHL career.Letang's future is also part of the wider conversation, although his age, contract commitments, and recent performances could make a potential trade more complicated.Bryan Rust and Rickard Rakell add to trade speculationBryan Rust and Rickard Rakell are two additional Pittsburgh players reportedly available for potential trade discussions.Both forwards could attract interest from teams looking to strengthen their offensive depth before the NHL trade deadline. Their situations also reflect the possibility of a broader roster transition if Pittsburgh continues struggling.Yohe indicated that he would be surprised if at least one of the two forwards remained with the Penguins beyond the March 1 trade deadline.For now, Dubas appears prepared to let his captain determine the outcome. Whether Crosby continues in Pittsburgh, considers retirement, or explores another NHL opportunity, his wishes are expected to guide the next chapter of his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vale - a team who can't lose at home, can't win away
articles.summary: Port Vale are on their best winning run in 66 years at home yet have not won away from Burslem all season - are they now on the up?
articles.body:
Port Vale are truly a team in top form right now - at Vale Park, that is.

Jon Brady's side are unbeaten in 10 home league and cup games this season - the last eight of them all victories.

It is their best run in Burslem since winning 10 league and cup games on the spin between October 1960 and March 1961.

Vale have knocked in 17 goals in their past four home games, a 5-0 win against Manchester City Under-21s in the Jersey Mike's Trophy, followed by three successive 4-2s - league victories over Rochdale and Accrington Stanley, either side of knocking National League side Scunthorpe United out of the FA Cup.

After a slow start this season, 'the Brady bunch' have risen to 17th in the League Two table - and are just four points off a play-off place.

The only downside to all that positivity is that the Vale are away this Saturday, at second-placed Barnet.

And that is the flip side of this season's mathematical equations - they are currently winless in eight away league and cup games, and have picked up just one point out of a possible 18.

But in-form Vale wing-back Jaheim Headley is still hopeful Saturday might be the day when it all changes.

"Doing well away from home is how you climb the table," he told BBC Radio Stoke.

"Barnet is not an easy place to go - but we're hoping to go down there and pick up a point at least. It would show everyone how serious we are."

That sort of positive thinking is welcome news to Vale boss Brady at a time when confidence is coursing through Midlands football like a flooded river.

Four sides from the region sit in the Championship's top five, including Vale's neighbours Stoke City, while Aston Villa are on the upturn in the top flight, Crewe Alexandra and Walsall are challenging again in League Two and even freshly-purchased Shrewsbury Town are beginning to look upwards again.

"The power of the mind is just an incredible thing," Vale boss Brady told BBC Radio Stoke. "You work hard first and foremost but, if you start to believe in what you do, then, my God...

"It's the connection. People are understanding each other's games. The players really are starting to lift to the level they can be.

"There would be no bigger statement than to go and get a result at Barnet. There's no tougher place to go in the league at the moment."

Headley, with two assists in the Cup win over Scunthorpe followed by his first two goals of the season against Accrington, is arguably the best example of that.

And he puts the improvement down to working on their finishing and now taking more of their chances.

"We were having issues early on with converting our chances," he added. "We were creating chances. We just weren't converting.

"But players have taken accountability. We've been doing more on the training ground. And we've turned the corner - and everyone's contributed.

"The coaching staff always talk about playing free in the final third. And we have the players who can unlock defences.

"The fans have been great too. When the fans are behind us we're a better team. We're forever grateful to them.

"There's no better feeling as a footballer than when you're playing well."
authors: Ged Scott and Phil Bowers - BBC Sport England

articles.title: Hincapie in advanced talks over new Arsenal deal
articles.summary: Arsenal are in advanced talks with defender Piero Hincapie over a new contract.
articles.body:
Arsenal are in advanced talks with defender Piero Hincapie over a new contract.

Hincapie, 24, joined the Gunners last summer from Bayer Leverkusen, initially on loan, with the Gunners activating an option to make the move permanent at the end of the season.

The Ecuador international has established himself as a key member of Mikel Arteta's squad, making 47 appearances in all competitions.

The versatile defender's existing deal still has over four years left to run - but he is now set to sign a 12-month extension on improved terms.

Elsewhere, the club intend to open talks with left-back Riccardo Calafiori, 24, over renewing his deal.

The Italy international has become a crucial part of Arteta's plans since his arrival from Bologna in 2024.

His current deal expires in the summer of 2029, but it is expected talks over an extension will begin in the not too distant future.

Arsenal are on a contract renewal drive, with the club set to confirm new deals for Jurrien Timber, Declan Rice and goalkeeper David Raya.

articles.title: Monday Night Therapy: Ohio State is Vulnerable…But Can Nebraska Actually Win?
articles.summary: On this episode of Monday Night Therapy, Minnie Hunt and Jon Johnston welcome Ohio State insider Ramsey from Eleven Warriors for an entertaining and surprisi...
articles.body:
On this episode of Monday Night Therapy, Minnie Hunt and Jon Johnston welcome Ohio State insider Ramsey from Eleven Warriors for an entertaining and surprisingly candid preview of Nebraska's upcoming showdown with the Buckeyes.

Fresh off Nebraska's 31–0 shutout of Rutgers, the crew examines whether the Huskers can capitalize on an Ohio State team struggling with inconsistency, questionable offensive line play, defensive personnel issues, and disastrous special teams.

Ramsey pulls no punches in his assessment of the Buckeyes, discussing coaching shortcomings, transfer portal disappointments, and the challenges of starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey. But Ohio State still possesses one enormous advantage: superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, whom Ramsey considers the best player in college football.

The conversation also explores the changing landscape of college football, including NIL, player development, coaching stability, expanded playoffs, and whether the transfer portal has fundamentally changed the sport.

Along the way, there's plenty of good-natured trash talk, frustration with modern college football, and even some shared disdain for Michigan.

Can Nebraska build on its momentum and pull off the upset in Lincoln? Ramsey calls Saturday's matchup essentially a coin flip, giving Husker fans reason for cautious optimism.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi confirms release of Usman and Umar Nurmagomedov from prison
articles.summary: Usman Nurmagomedov and Umar Nurmagomedov have been released from Abu Dhabi jail just days after receiving six month sentences for attacking former UFC bantam...
articles.body:
Usman Nurmagomedov and Umar Nurmagomedov have been released from Abu Dhabi jail just days after receiving six month sentences for attacking former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili.

Usman Nurmagomedov, the PFL lightweight champion, was in Abu Dhabi to support his brother Umar in his Real American Freestyle match against Urijah Faber. He got a little sidetracked on that front when he and several teammates spotted Dvalishvili at the athlete hotel and jumped him. Footage of the brawl quickly hit the internet, and just as quickly everyone involved was arrested by Abu Dhabi authorities.

Six month sentences and $82,000 fines were issued to the eight men who instigated the attack. Four days later, a deal was reached to reduce the sentences and deport them with $41,000 fines. We're still sorting out just what happened … there are reports that Khabib Nurmagomedov travelled to Abu Dhabi to secure the release of his cousins and teammates, other reports of million dollar payments behind the scenes, and even more whispers of a gag order to never speak of the incident in public.

None of that is confirmed. But Abu Dhabi authorities did release a statement confirming the release for totally legitimate reasons.

"The Criminal Court has reduced the sentences of eight defendants involved in a mass brawl at a hotel, filming it and causing public disorder following earlier disputes between them," the Abu Dhabi Judicial Department statement read. "The revised penalty is a fine of Dh150,000 for each defendant, following reconciliation and mutual withdrawal of claims between the parties, as well as an appeal by the victim to the Abu Dhabi Government for their release."

The two victims of the attack, Merab Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili, both refused to press charges and repeatedly called for the release of the men who attacked them. That seems to have played a big part in allowing Abu Dhabi to show leniency to Team Nurmagomedov.

"The ruling is consistent with the legal framework governing the criminal case and considers the settlement between the parties and their withdrawal of mutual claims and disputes arising from the incident."

This is a big win for Usman and Umar Nurmagomedov, whose careers were looking like they'd be badly derailed due to their thuggish stupidity. Six months in prison would have screwed up their year, not to mention the possibility of being barred from entering the U.A.E. and possibly other countries due to criminal charges.

We'll keep you updated as further details emerge from the situation.
